products.blurb: Choose between mount entry, maintenance, remounting and attack sections instead of treating every loss of mount as the same problem.

guide.display_title: Gordon Ryan: Mount Maintenance and Attacks

fits: You reach mount but lose it during a bridge, a recovery attempt or the start of an attack.
consider_alternative_if: For lower- and upper-body riding tools across several top positions, compare Craig Jones’s Power Ride.

includes: Mount entries and a dedicated maintenance volume.
Remounting from three-quarter mount and responses to bridge or knee-elbow recovery.
Arm-isolation and submission topics, followed by rolling and commentary.
limits: Mount is the organizing position; side-control and north-south maintenance are covered by a separate course.

start_here.title: Distinguish arrival from the first escape attempt
start_here.task: Recall one mount loss and note whether it happened while arriving, during a bridge, or while starting an attack. Compare the outline’s Countering a Bridge entries in Volumes 1 and 5 with Volume 3’s Countering a Push & Bridge. Their surrounding chapters identify different study contexts. With access, start in Volume 2’s maintenance introduction and select the relevant context afterward.
